title: Rockstar UK union vote could cover 1,600+ workers, says IWGB
description: The IWGB says a Rockstar UK union recognition vote around the GTA 6 console launch could cover over 1,600 staff below director level, per Rock Paper Shotgun.

body.text: The union organising UK-based Rockstar Games developers says its proposed bargaining unit would cover more than 1,600 workers, according to Rock Paper Shotgun. The Independent Workers of Great Britain (IWGB) says that is nearly everyone at Rockstar's UK studios below director level. A recognition vote is due around the console launch of GTA 6 on November 19th, which makes the timing hard to ignore.

Organisers have said a successful vote would create "the biggest recognised union in the UK games sector." When asked to put a number on that claim, the IWGB told Game File, as reported by Rock Paper Shotgun, that the bargaining unit would exceed 1,600 workers.

Rock Paper Shotgun notes that the director level typically marks the line between regular staff and senior management. So the proposed unit would take in almost everyone beneath that tier at Rockstar's UK studios.
Who is in, and who is not

The union is limited to the UK. Rockstar staff in other countries, including the US and India, would not be part of it. Rock Paper Shotgun cites recent Bloomberg reporting that puts Rockstar's total headcount at over 4,700 people across 12 locations worldwide.
For Indian readers, that means the vote has no direct effect on Rockstar's staff in India. It is still a significant data point for how large studios handle labour organising.
According to Rock Paper Shotgun, the recognition votes will run from November 12th to November 26th. That starts a week before GTA 6 arrives on consoles.

Rockstar Game Workers Union Committee Member Shanti Easton-Steel said in an IWGB press release that the vote is about getting honesty and openness on decisions that affect staff. She pointed to several concerns:

items: Overtime pay policies she described as uneven and ever-changing
Job security after the game's release

body.text: A separate dispute is also reaching a head around the same time. An employment tribunal is examining Rockstar's decision last year to fire 34 mostly UK-based staff, according to Rock Paper Shotgun.

Rockstar has accused the dismissed workers of risking the leak of confidential information while posting on a Discord server set up by union organisers. The IWGB accuses Rockstar of acting out of a desire to bust the union. These are competing claims, and the tribunal has yet to rule on them.

Keep an eye on the voting window from November 12th to 26th and on whether Rockstar publicly responds to the IWGB's figures. The tribunal's progress matters too, since it could shape how the vote is perceived. If recognition goes through, the UK games sector will have a new benchmark for what organised developer labour looks like.

sources.title: Rockstar developer union could end up over 1,600 workers strong and encompass nearly all UK staff below senior management, IWGB claim
